name: FORTRESS
description: Fortress is a challenging open-information Solitaire (Patience) game characterized by its unique building rules and lack of a draw pile. Unlike many other solitaires, Fortress allows players to build sequences both up and down within the tableau, provided they follow suit. All cards are dealt at the start; the top card of each column is available. Empty tableau spaces may be filled with any available card. It is often cited as a game of skill rather than luck, where planning several moves ahead is essential for victory.

content.text: Fortress is a challenging open-information Solitaire (Patience) game characterized by its unique building rules and lack of a draw pile. Unlike many other solitaires, Fortress allows players to build sequences both up and down within the tableau, provided they follow suit. All cards are dealt at the start; the top card of each column is available. Empty tableau spaces may be filled with any available card. It is often cited as a game of skill rather than luck, where planning several moves ahead is essential for victory.

Fortress, also known as 'Chessboard' in some regional histories, is an old European solitaire that likely predates the 20th century. Its name is derived from the appearance of the ten columns of cards, which resemble the battlements of a castle's fortress.
One player only. Fortress is a patience (solitaire) game; the entire deck is laid out at the start and the single player moves cards between the tableau columns and the four foundations.
Deal 52 cards face-up into 10 columns: two columns of 6 cards (one on the left, one on the right) and eight columns of 5 cards. Four foundation spaces in the centre for aces.

items.text: Chessboard: Played like Fortress except the player may freely choose the starting rank of all four foundations. Building can go round-the-corner (aces may be placed on kings and vice versa).
